content.text: Station's pool is capped at 10 connections, and wait time jumps to the 30-second timeout in the abnormal window. To trace how the failure climbs toward users, I'll join caller and callee spans on parent ID and count error status by service pair.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, c.service_name caller, s.service_name callee, count(*) n, avg(CASE WHEN s.attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) callee_err, avg(CASE WHEN c.attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) caller_err, approx_quantile(c.duration,0.95)/1e6 caller_p95 FROM abnormal_traces s JOIN abnormal_traces c ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id WHERE s.attr_span_kind='Server' AND c.attr_span_kind='Client' AND c.service_name<>s.service_name GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY caller, callee

A second investigator, starting fresh with the same tools, tested the kind of each fault in your draft answer. Their findings:

### `ts-station-service`: you said `database_call_failed`. They conclude `network_partition` (confidence: medium).
Scope: Affected: ts-station-service's database access over its JDBC connection to mysql. Every DB-touching route (GET /stations/id/{name} and POST /stations/idlist) stalls to about 30 s and fails, and the station's connection pool is exhausted, while station's own alive-ness is intact. Not affected: station's metrics and logs keep flowing, mysql still emits its normal metric volume, and station's non-DB traffic (the normal Client span 'SELECT ts.station') stays at about 1 ms. The cut is on the station-to-mysql link; the data does not show which end of it.
Ruled out:
- `database_call_failed`: The failures are connection-level, not SQL-layer: 'Communications link failure ... The driver has not received any packets from the server', SQLState 08S01 and 08003 (connection closed), 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms'. A database_call_failed fault would show SQL-layer exceptions on particular statements while others succeed. Here every DB-touching route stalls to about 30 s (both station routes go from p50 about 3 ms to about 30,010 ms), so it is the whole connection that is affected, not one statement.
- `pod_unavailable`: Station keeps emitting: about 313 to 321 metric rows per minute and about 370 to 51 logs per minute, all in the failure path. Its Server spans still arrive (39 POST idlist and 7 GET id spans in the incident, slow but present). MySQL emits the same 1,056 metric rows in normal and abnormal periods. Both ends are alive, so the pod is not gone.
- `database_call_slow`: The slowdown is not a steady extra on particular statements with the connection healthy. It is a 30 s timeout on all DB-touching routes plus link-failure errors on the connection, and the pool wait is capped at the Hikari 30 s timeout. That is a connection fault, not a slow statement.
Evidence:
- Station's 'SELECT station' spans are Internal, not Client. In the abnormal period 30 spans end in Error at p50 about 30,004 ms and p95 about 30,007 ms, and 9 are Unset with p50 about 7,234 ms. In the normal period 587 Unset spans run at p50 about 1.2 ms and p95 about 2.1 ms. The only Client span, 'SELECT ts.station', is normal at p95 about 0.7 to 1.0 ms. So the DB calls stall for the full 30 s timeout, and the lead's 'DB span' is an Internal span inside station.

- Abnormal station logs are connection-level: 'Communications link failure ... The driver has not received any packets from the server' (35), 'SQL Error: 0, SQLState: 08S01' (35), 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms' (31), and 'No operations allowed after connection closed' (1). Logs start at about 23:36:42 and run to 23:40:01. Normal logs are only INFO query messages. No SQL-layer exception text appears.
  `SELECT 'abn' p, level, message, count(*) n, min(time) first_t, max(time) last_t FROM abnormal_logs WHERE service_name='ts-station-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', level, message, count(*), min(time), max(time) FROM normal_logs WHERE service_name='ts-station-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY n DESC`
- MySQL has 1,056 metric rows in both periods, so it is alive. Station's Server spans for both routes are present in the incident but slow: POST idlist 39 spans with p50 about 30,009 ms (normal 587 spans at p50 about 3.7 ms); GET id 7 spans with p50 about 30,010 ms (normal 894 at about 3.2 ms). kind_checks.scope: Affected: ts-station-service's database access over its JDBC connection to mysql. Every DB-touching route (GET /stations/id/{name} and POST /stations/idlist) stalls to about 30 s and fails, and the station's connection pool is exhausted, while station's own alive-ness is intact. Not affected: station's metrics and logs keep flowing, mysql still emits its normal metric volume, and station's non-DB traffic (the normal Client span 'SELECT ts.station') stays at about 1 ms. The cut is on the station-to-mysql link; the data does not show which end of it.

ruled_out.why: The failures are connection-level, not SQL-layer: 'Communications link failure ... The driver has not received any packets from the server', SQLState 08S01 and 08003 (connection closed), 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms'. A database_call_failed fault would show SQL-layer exceptions on particular statements while others succeed. Here every DB-touching route stalls to about 30 s (both station routes go from p50 about 3 ms to about 30,010 ms), so it is the whole connection that is affected, not one statement.

Station keeps emitting: about 313 to 321 metric rows per minute and about 370 to 51 logs per minute, all in the failure path. Its Server spans still arrive (39 POST idlist and 7 GET id spans in the incident, slow but present). MySQL emits the same 1,056 metric rows in normal and abnormal periods. Both ends are alive, so the pod is not gone.

The slowdown is not a steady extra on particular statements with the connection healthy. It is a 30 s timeout on all DB-touching routes plus link-failure errors on the connection, and the pool wait is capped at the Hikari 30 s timeout. That is a connection fault, not a slow statement.

In the abnormal period 30 spans end in Error at p50 about 30,004 ms and p95 about 30,007 ms, and 9 are Unset with p50 about 7,234 ms. In the normal period 587 Unset spans run at p50 about 1.2 ms and p95 about 2.1 ms. The only Client span, 'SELECT ts.station', is normal at p95 about 0.7 to 1.0 ms. So the DB calls stall for the full 30 s timeout, and the lead's 'DB span' is an Internal span inside station.

**Verdict: `database_call_failed` is not supported. The telemetry points to a network fault on the link between `ts-station-service` and MySQL, which is the `network_partition` / `network_loss` equivalence class. Confidence: moderate.**

**Evidence against `database_call_failed`:**

- **The errors are connection-level, not SQL-layer.** The logs show `Communications link failure ... The driver has not received any packets from the server`, SQLState `08S01` and `08003` (connection closed), `Unable to acquire JDBC Connection`, and `HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 30000ms`. The boundary rules put connection-level errors and pool waits on the network side. A `database_call_failed` would show SQL-layer exceptions on particular statements while others succeed.
- **Every DB-touching route hangs, not particular statements.** Both station Server routes (`GET .../stations/id/{name}` and `POST .../stations/idlist`) go from p50 about 3 ms to p50 about 30,010 ms. Their p95s sit at about 30,014 and 30,053 ms. Failures are not confined to one statement.
- **The timing is a hang to timeout, not a fast fail.** Calls wait about 30 s and then fail, which fits a cut or hung link rather than a statement that throws at once.
- **Both ends are alive.** Station keeps emitting metrics (313 → 321 rows/min) and logs (370 → 51/min, all in the failure path). MySQL emits the same 1,056 metric rows in both periods. This is not a pod fault at either end.
- **The lead's spans are Internal, not DB Client spans.** The "SELECT station" spans are Internal spans inside station's process. The only Client span named "SELECT ts.station" is normal (p95 about 0.7 ms) and drops in volume only because callers stopped sending. So the DB call itself is not traced separately.

**What the evidence does not show:**

- I did not confirm the station↔MySQL per-connection `hubble_*` drop or flow counts. The hubble rows I pulled did not include that pair, so I cannot cite per-connection drops either way.
- The data does not separate `network_partition` from `network_loss`. The logs show a hard cut (no packets received), but I did not look at the loss-shaped tail on that connection, so I am not claiming partition over loss beyond the equivalence class.
- Station's Unset "SELECT station" spans have a p50 of about 7 s, so some calls do complete slowly. That fits an intermittent or saturating connection, not a steady statement-level fault.
